page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 124 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent disk operations.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, with Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU scores reaching the top 10% and top 25% respectively. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, which contribute to strong performance in vector calculations, cryptography, and image processing. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier, while single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show top-tier execution speeds.

From a resource density perspective, the c4d-standard-32 offers a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high single-thread performance without the overhead of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled from compute, allowing for flexible scaling. This instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, static web serving, text and image processing, and moderate-scale language model inference.

It is highly suitable for software compilation, image and text processing, static web serving, and moderate machine learning inference workloads.
